notes:
Honda and Acura cars that use 29-bit CAN on the OBD-II socket (ELM327 protocol 7, 500 kbit/s): the Accord, Accord Hybrid, Civic, Clarity, CR-V, Fit (Jazz), Insight, Pilot, Ridgeline and ZR-V and the Acura Integra, RDX and TLX that OBDb has repositories for, and the wider range opendbc lists (among them the HR-V), with UDS service 22. A unit's request identifier is 18DAxxF1 (xx the unit, F1 the tester) and its reply comes from 18DAF1xx.

Every row is an address pair and nothing more: no data identifier or scaling is shipped, because the only sources are other projects' signal definitions, which this repository does not copy. Each row cites every archived OBDb repository that lists its pair. OBDb writes a unit as DAxx, which this profile reads as 18DAxxF1: its schema (https://github.com/OBDb/.schemas/blob/main/signals.json, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261116150735/https://github.com/OBDb/.schemas/blob/main/signals.json) describes the header only as a three- or four-digit hex identifier and does not say so, and the reading rests on opendbc using the full form for the same units. Where the two sources differ: OBDb marks 0x28 as ABS and also lists 0x2A as ABS, while opendbc has only 0x28 (as vsa); OBDb has rows opendbc does not (0x0E, 0x11, 0x1D, 0x26, 0x2A, 0x01, 0x15, 0x16), and opendbc has units OBDb does not (0x0B, 0x2B, 0x61, 0xEF, 0xB0, 0xB5, the forward camera and radar). opendbc's 0x10 and 0x60 are listed as extra units its query software probes, not fingerprint units. OBDb's DBEF rows (Accord Hybrid, Clarity, Insight and ZR-V) have no reply identifier, so they are left out. The charger at 0x15 and second battery unit at 0x16 rest on the Clarity repository alone.

opendbc lists a European CR-V and a Civic diesel among its cars, but most of what both sources describe is sold in North America and Japan. A UK or European Honda may lay its units out differently, with some units absent or on another identifier, and the 29-bit scheme may not be on the OBD-II socket at all behind a gateway. opendbc's queries come from a comma.ai device wired into the car, which is not the OBD-II socket. opendbc's own comment says the forward camera does not support being queried in parallel with another unit and that the radar at 18DAB0F1 often fails to respond. Treat every row as unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows it answering. The default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened.
